units.notes: The planned retirement year of 2024 has passed, but the unit is still in operation. The owner's 2022 environmental report plans to replace its old engines with new ones, not to close the unit. Details are in the questions.

No change found. The 2022 environmental report describes a new building with 8 gas engines, so pre-construction is still reasonable. I could not read any newer document that gives a start date, the engine make or a construction start. The permit office and its notice pages were blocked or empty.

qa.recommendation: Clear the planned retirement year of 2024 and consider recording the engine replacement in the status detail.
qa.note: The 2022 environmental report for EVC 1, EVC 2 and EVC 3 says the nine existing engines of each of the first two blocks are to be swapped for nine new engines of 5.28 MW electric each. That would raise each block from about 34.9 MW to 47.5 MW electric. The report names Bergen Engines type B36:45 L9AG1 as the expected make. It says nothing about closing either block. The regulator's list of June 2026 still shows the old 3.8 MW engines as in operation. I could not find a date for the swap.

qa.note: GEM has 10 engines of 3.9 MW, which gives 39.0 MW. The environmental report says nine engines are installed and ten were permitted, at about 34.9 MW electric in total. The regulator's list shows nine engines of 3.83 MW gross, about 34.5 MW. The same list shows nine engines for EVC1 at 3.88 MW gross, about 35.0 MW, while GEM has 8 engines and 31.2 MW. Both blocks may be undercounted or overcounted in GEM. I did not change the values because the brief did not ask for a capacity check on these blocks.
